body.en: Unit 4 is a capstone: functions as dynamic models where parameters control behaviour. This includes inverse functions, composite functions, implicit functions, and parametric curves — all viewed as tools for modelling the real world.

Composition: \((f\circ g)(x)=f(g(x)).\) Domain of \(f\circ g\) = domain of \(g\) restricted so that \(g(x)\) is in the domain of \(f.\)

Inverse: \(f^{-1}\) exists iff \(f\) is one-to-one (passes horizontal line test).

\[f(f^{-1}(x))=x\quad\text{and}\quad f^{-1}(f(x))=x.\]

Graph of \(f^{-1}\) is the reflection of \(f\) over \(y=x.\)

body.en:
A piecewise function uses different rules for different intervals of the domain. Check continuity at breakpoints: left- and right-hand values must agree.

Implicit function: defined by a relation \(F(x,y)=0\) rather than explicitly as \(y=f(x)\). A circle \(x^2+y^2=r^2\) is implicit.

A parametric curve is given by \(x=f(t),\;y=g(t)\) for parameter \(t.\)

Eliminating the parameter: solve one equation for \(t\), substitute into the other. Or use a Pythagorean identity when \(x=a\cos t,\;y=b\sin t\).

\[\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=\cos^2 t+\sin^2 t=1\quad\text{→ ellipse}.\]

problem.en: A projectile: \(x=30t,\;y=40t-5t^2\). (a) Eliminate \(t\) to find the Cartesian equation. (b) Find the maximum height.

solution.en:
(a) \(t=x/30\). Then \(y=40\!\left(\dfrac{x}{30}\right)-5\!\left(\dfrac{x}{30}\right)^2=\dfrac{4x}{3}-\dfrac{x^2}{180}.\)

(b) Complete the square or use vertex formula: \(t_{\max}=40/(2\cdot5)=4.\) \(y_{\max}=40(4)-5(16)=160-80=80\) m.

figure.title: Parametric Ellipse: x(t) = 2 cos(t), y(t) = 3 sin(t)

caption.en: Parametric curve $x(t) = 2\cos t$, $y(t) = 3\sin t$ for $0 \le t \le 2\pi$. Eliminating the parameter via the identity $\cos^2 t + \sin^2 t = 1$ yields the Cartesian ellipse $\frac{x^2}{4} + \frac{y^2}{9} = 1$ with semi-minor axis 2 and semi-major axis 3.

label.en: ▲ AP Exam Traps & Pitfalls — Functions Involving Parameters

body.en:
• Horizontal Line Test & Domain Restrictions: A function only possesses an inverse function \(f^{-1}\) if it is strictly one-to-one. For quadratic or even-degree polynomial functions, the domain must be restricted (e.g. \(x \ge 0\)) to produce an invertible branch.
  • Domain Restrictions in Composition: The domain of \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\) is not just the domain of \(f\). You must first require \(x\) to be in the domain of \(g\), AND \(g(x)\) must fall within the domain of \(f\).
  • Orientation and Speed in Parametric Curves: Unlike Cartesian graphs \(y = f(x)\), parametric curves \((x(t), y(t))\) possess a direction of motion (orientation) as parameter \(t\) increases. Eliminating the parameter can lose this directional information or fail to reflect finite endpoints when \(t\) is restricted to an interval \([a, b]\).
  • Matrix Transformations are Non-Commutative: In 2D geometric matrix transformations, applying transformation \(A\) followed by transformation \(B\) results in the product matrix \(BA\), NOT \(AB\). Matrix multiplication is not commutative!

question.en: A parametric curve is defined by \(x(t) = 2\cos t\) and \(y(t) = 3\sin t\) for \(0 \le t \le 2\pi\). (a) Eliminate the parameter to obtain a Cartesian equation relating \(x\) and \(y\). (b) Identify the conic curve, its vertices, co-vertices, and state the domain and range.

solution.en:
(a) Parameter elimination: From the parametric equations, isolate the trigonometric components: \(\cos t = \dfrac{x}{2}\) and \(\sin t = \dfrac{y}{3}\). Apply the fundamental Pythagorean identity \(\cos^2 t + \sin^2 t = 1\): \[\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{y}{3}\right)^2 = 1 \implies \dfrac{x^2}{4} + \dfrac{y^2}{9} = 1.\]

(b) Geometric attributes: This is a vertical ellipse centered at \((0, 0)\). The major axis lies along the \(y\)-axis with vertices at \((0, \pm 3)\) (semi-major axis \(a = 3\)). The minor axis lies along the \(x\)-axis with co-vertices at \((\pm 2, 0)\) (semi-minor axis \(b = 2\)). Domain: \([-2, 2]\); Range: \([-3, 3]\).

question.en: Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{4x - 5}{2x + 1}\) for \(x \neq -\frac{1}{2}\). (a) Find the formula for the inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\). (b) State the domain and range of \(f^{-1}(x)\). (c) Verify that \(f(f^{-1}(x)) = x\).

solution.en:
(a) Inverse derivation: Set \(y = \dfrac{4x - 5}{2x + 1}\). Solve for \(x\) in terms of \(y\): \(y(2x + 1) = 4x - 5 \Rightarrow 2xy + y = 4x - 5 \Rightarrow 2xy - 4x = -y - 5 \Rightarrow x(2y - 4) = -(y + 5)\). Thus \(x = \dfrac{-(y + 5)}{2y - 4} = \dfrac{y + 5}{4 - 2y}\). Swapping variables: \(f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{x + 5}{4 - 2x}\) (or \(\dfrac{-x - 5}{2x - 4}\)).

(b) Domain and Range: The denominator of \(f^{-1}\) is zero when \(4 - 2x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2\). Domain of \(f^{-1}\): \((-\infty, 2) \cup (2, \infty)\). The range of \(f^{-1}\) equals the domain of \(f\): \((-\infty, -1/2) \cup (-1/2, \infty)\).

(c) Verification: \(f(f^{-1}(x)) = \dfrac{4\left(\frac{x+5}{4-2x}\right) - 5}{2\left(\frac{x+5}{4-2x}\right) + 1} = \dfrac{4(x+5) - 5(4-2x)}{2(x+5) + (4-2x)} = \dfrac{4x + 20 - 20 + 10x}{2x + 10 + 4 - 2x} = \dfrac{14x}{14} = x\). \(\checkmark\)
